import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Handle missing values for 'Income' as it's crucial for this visualization
# It's common to have a few NaN values in real-world income data
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Calculate the total amount spent on all products
mnt_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col.startswith('Mnt')]
df['Total_Mnt'] = df[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
sns.set_context("notebook", font_scale=1.2)

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Income, Total Spending, and Campaign Response
# We use 'hue' to differentiate customers based on their response to the last campaign
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='Income', y='Total_Mnt', hue='Response',
                palette='viridis', alpha=0.7, s=60, edgecolor='w', linewidth=0.5)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Customer Spending vs. Income, by Last Campaign Response', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Amount Spent on Products', fontsize=14)

# Improve legend for better understanding
handles, labels = plt.gca().get_legend_handles_labels()
new_labels = ['Did Not Respond' if label == '0' else 'Responded' for label in labels]
plt.legend(handles=handles, labels=new_labels, title='Last Campaign Response',
           bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust plot layout to prevent labels/legend from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
